subject: tech
title: Circuits and Switches
about: A circuit is a loop that electricity travels around: a battery, two wires and a bulb make one, and the light comes on only when the loop is closed (K2-CS-02). A switch opens and closes the loop, and a gap or loose wire is a bug you fix by checking the connections (K2-CS-04). Circuits are a bridge topic from Grade 4 science, so read it together; a flashlight is a circuit in a tube you can open up and look at.
tip: Open a flashlight together, take the battery out and put it back, and say the loop out loud: battery, wire, bulb, wire, back to the battery.

cards.q: Electricity travels around a loop to light a bulb. What is the loop called?
cards.note: A circuit is a loop for electricity: out of the battery, through the bulb, and back again.

cards.q: A battery, two wires and a bulb are joined in a loop. What happens to the bulb?
cards.note: Battery, wire, bulb, wire, back to the battery. The loop is closed, so the bulb lights.

cards.q: The light comes on only when the loop is what?
cards.note: Closed means no gaps. Electricity can go all the way round.

cards.q: One wire comes loose. There is a gap in the loop. What does the bulb do?
cards.note: A gap means the electricity cannot get round. No loop, no light.

cards.q: What opens and closes the loop so you can turn the light on and off?
cards.note: A switch is a tiny gate in the loop. Closed: light on. Open: light off.

cards.q: You flip the switch and the light goes off. What did the switch do to the loop?
cards.note: Off means the switch opened a gap. On means it closed the gap.

cards.q: You flip the switch and the light comes on. What did the switch do to the loop?
cards.note: Closed loop, light on. Open loop, light off.

cards.q: Your bulb stays dark. What do you check first?
cards.note: A loose wire is a bug in the circuit. Check each connection, one at a time, like debugging.

cards.q: You find the loose wire and hook it back on. What happens?
cards.note: Fix the gap, close the loop, and the light comes back. That is debugging a circuit.

cards.q: Wires are made of metal inside. Why?
cards.note: Metal lets electricity flow. We say metal is a conductor.

cards.q: Wires have a plastic cover. What is it for?
cards.note: Plastic does not let electricity through, so the cover keeps it inside the wire and off your hands.

cards.q: The light switch on your wall does what to a circuit?
cards.note: Flip up: the loop closes and the ceiling light comes on. Flip down: a gap opens, light off.

cards.q: You take the bulb out and put a buzzer in the loop. What happens when the loop closes?
cards.note: A buzzer, a tiny motor or a bulb can all sit in the loop. Each turns electricity into something: sound, spin or light.

cards.q: You put a small motor in the circuit. What does it do when the loop closes?
cards.note: A motor turns electricity into spinning. Fans and toy cars have motors inside.

cards.q: A flashlight is a circuit in a tube. What are the parts inside?
cards.note: Push the switch: the loop closes, and electricity goes from the battery to the bulb.

cards.q: Which of these lets electricity through?
cards.note: Metal conducts. Plastic and rubber do not, which is why they cover wires and plugs.

cards.q: Which one is for grown-ups only?
cards.note: A little battery circuit is a safe thing to learn with a grown-up. Wall outlets carry much more electricity and are only for grown-ups.

cards.q: The circuit is battery, wire, bulb, wire. Where does the electricity start?
cards.note: The battery is the push. Electricity leaves one end, goes round the loop and comes back to the other end.
